newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur VGO softer, low. [CORRECTED 21:29 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur VGO softer, low. [CORRECTED 21:29 GMT]

text.p: High sulphur VGO prices were softer in thin post-holiday trade and prices for low sulphur remained weak, slipping as poor U.S. demand limited trans-Atlantic arbitrage trade, traders said on Wednesday.

Russian cargoes and local production continued to satisfy demand from high sulphur VGO buyers in mainland Europe but traders said some stand-off caused by weaker crude and generally weaker sentiment was developing between buyers and sellers.
High sulphur prices were around $3 (corrects from $1) per tonne lower at around the $131-$133 (corrects from $133-$135) level for fob cargoes.

Weaker U.S. prices with several players seen long on product there continued to hold low sulphur product out of North America, although one trader said he believed the arbitrage was still open for larger cargoes heading west.
Low sulphur VGO cargoes drifted $3-4 (corrects from $1-2) to around $136/$139 (corrects from $138-$141) fob NWE. Barge markets were quiet -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
